Subject: Post-demo: performance & SLO confirmation for Aurora Health

Hi Priya / Tim —

Thanks again for running through the demo yesterday. Quick recap of the performance constraints you called out and the items we agreed to validate as part of the pilot. Wanted to confirm these back so we’re aligned before scheduling the ops load test.

Key SLO targets (requested by Aurora product team):
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms for 512-token inference (single-shot text generation; production prompt distribution attached)
- Streaming: p50 per-chunk <= 60ms for 256-token streaming responses, chunk size ~64 tokens
- Throughput: sustained 400 req/s for peak window (30 min sustained), with burst up to 1,200 req/s for up to 2 minutes
- Concurrency: 200–250 concurrent active sessions (long-lived streaming + KV cache)
- Cold starts: first-token p95 <= 400ms on dedicated nodes; acceptable fallback to smaller variant if hard budget limit reached
- Cache: target KV/prefix cache hit 30–40% on conversational traffic; measure impact on effective latency/throughput

Operational asks from Redwood (next steps we proposed):
1) Aurora to share a representative request distribution + sample prompts (we received the sample file; thanks)
2) Redwood to run a 30-minute sustained load test matching the distribution (we’ll provide a short playbook)
3) Tech workshop (1 hour) to validate streaming setup and fallback policy — please propose times next week
4) Attachments: SLO checklist (attached) and streaming recommendations PDF (attached)

Notes / constraints we flagged: quantized model variants will reduce GPU memory and can change per-token latency distribution — we’ll evaluate p95 tradeoffs during the load run. We’ll also surface token-unit estimates for pricing impact if you want to scope cost during pilot.

Please confirm the SLO numbers above and call out any changes. If these align, Marcus and I will schedule the load run and share the ops playbook + test harness.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Priya —

Great questions, answers below (TL;DR: our numbers in the checklist are end-to-end for the request path we control; we'll instrument for VPC egress in the pilot):

- Streaming p50: the 60ms number in the checklist is target for end-to-end server-side emission of a chunk (includes model decode + Redwood runtime serialization). It does not include cross-region network egress. For pilot acceptance we can include an additional network hop budget (we recommend +20–50ms depending on VPC setup).

- GPU footprint: Marcus — ballpark is 2–4 A100-equivalent GPUs for the sustained 400 req/s baseline on the recommended quantized variant, with 1–2 additional GPUs for burst headroom. We'll confirm exact sizing after we run the representative load profile.

- Cold starts: we'll include the 400ms p95 cold-start target in the acceptance checklist. If we observe higher numbers, automatic fallback to a lower-memory variant will be part of the fallback policy.

- Pricing: rough estimate for planning only — ~USD 35–45 per 1M tokens for the pilot configuration (mix of generation + streaming); final numbers vary by token mix and quantization. We’ll provide a more precise run-based estimate after the load test.

Actions I’ll take this week:

- Kick off internal load test prep and share the playbook + test harness repo link
- Update the SLO checklist with the network budget note and GPU sizing estimate (attached updated checklist)

If that all sounds good I’ll set the workshop invite and the test window.

Cheers,

Quick technical note from my side on streaming and KV cache setup — copying the relevant portion of the internal ops playbook below.

- Streaming configuration:
  * Chunk size: 64 tokens per chunk with server-side flush after chunk completes. This minimizes jitter and keeps p50 low.
  * Write-behind batching: enable small (10–20ms) coalescing window for high-concurrency traffic to maintain throughput without blowing up latency.

- KV/prefix cache recommendations:
  * Use a two-level cache: in-process LRU for hot prefixes + remote shared cache for cross-worker hits. Aim for 30%+ hit-rate on hot conversation flows.
  * Cache TTLs: 60–300s depending on tech stack; tune during the pilot run.

I’ve dropped the ops playbook and a short runbook link here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3cAuroraSLO

If you want, we can include a short benchmark target table in the workshop (p50/p95 per-chunk, per-token CPU/GPU time) so your SREs have clear acceptance gates.

—Marcus
